acct_note: each isend pays its own link latency (n/B + L per isend); bandwidth accrues per chunk

candidate_accountings.per_isend: plugin charges n_chunk/B + L per isend; model latency factor scaled by pieces-per-phase
candidate_accountings.per_logical_transfer: plugin charges n_chunk/B per isend plus L once per logical phase; keeps model per-phase alpha

distortion_note: per-isend charge inflates M2->M3 adjacent delta by 22.9% of gate 35% budget (PI analysis); per-logical-transfer keeps model per-phase alpha
negative_control: missing/zero-bw link returns -1/-2 and run fails loudly (tested separately)

accounting_unit_analysis.note_pieces: 4MB run (4 isends total, 2 per rank): 1 piece per channel per phase. At gate size (32MB) pieces-per-phase scales with NCCL chunk count; exact count requires a successful 32MB run (deferred due to fabric timeout).

candidate_A_per_isend.model_change: latency factor lf scaled by pieces-per-phase P

candidate_B_per_logical_transfer.plugin_charge: n_chunk/B per isend + L once per logical phase (latency distributed across chunks)

accounting_unit_analysis.decision: per_isend (candidate A) — chosen because (1) each isend is a real transfer that pays link latency in the plugin's measured path, (2) the trace records the unit per transfer (acct=per_isend) so a reader sees it without inferring, (3) candidate B requires phase-boundary detection in the plugin which is not available without changing NCCL's call pattern. The mismatch between candidates is reported, not hidden; the gate's 35% budget is not silently consumed.
accounting_unit_analysis.final_decision: per_isend (candidate A): each isend pays n_chunk/B + L; model latency factor scaled by P (pieces per phase). Unit stated in trace as acct=per_isend. Both candidates + 4-config distortion in candidate_accountings/distortion_note.

payload_size_decision.rationale: fabric carries 2 MiB with margin (run succeeded R0=R1=0, 4 isends per rank, no timeout); 2 MiB is in the model's bandwidth regime (bw_term >= 10*lat_term at 10 Gbps: 168 us vs 10 us). 32 MiB timed out (queueing: 8 slots x 1MB, 25 Gbps gives 2.8ms queue wait vs 5ms deadline).
payload_size_decision.evidence_run: trace_pkb2mb.log (4 isends per rank, all completed)
payload_size_decision.rejected: 32 MiB (timed out), 8 MiB (timed out), 4 MiB not tested
payload_size_decision.re_admission_note: gate's config set (gpu-sim-gmc) must be re-admitted at 2 MiB; margins recomputed.

fabric_timeout_diagnosis.conclusion: queue wait (6.4ms) exceeds deadline (5ms) at 10 Gbps -> timeout. Confirmed: 2 MiB (1 piece) succeeds, 8 MiB+ times out.

bytes_finding: At 1 MiB, plugin sends S per rank (1048576 B) but model predicts 2S per rank (2097152 B). NCCL's byte count changes with size: 2S at 4 KiB, S at 1 MiB+. Model byte factor (2.0 at n=2) only matches at small sizes. This is a model error to be addressed by 8sy/gate, not a pkb defect.
time_finding: Time agreement at 1 MiB: plugin 899 us vs model 1718 us (48% error) due to byte count mismatch (S vs 2S). At 4 KiB: 0% error, exact bytes (latency regime).
item9_status: NOT MET at bandwidth-regime size: bytes diverge (S vs 2S) at 1 MiB+. Only 4 KiB (latency regime) gives exact agreement. Reported as finding, not widened.
